1 عَزَقَ الأَرْضَ , aor.
عَزِقَ , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. عَزْقٌ, (S, O, Msb,) He clave, or furrowed, the earth, or land, with the implement called مِعْزَقَةٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and مِعْزَقٌ. (S, O, K.) ―
-b2- And He dug the earth until the water came forth from it. (TA.) ―
-b3- The verb is [said to be] used only in relation to the earth, or land. (S, O, Msb, K.) [But] لَا تَعْزِقُوا occurs in a trad. as meaning Cut not ye (لَا تَقْطَعُو). (TA.) ―
-b4- العَزْقُ metonymically used as meaning The act of eating is post-classical. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
